chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man whose tailbone was broken, so that he could no longer control his anus. What compensation is due in it? He said: “The full diyah.”
He said: And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with a slave-girl and caused ifda' to her, and when she came into that condition she would not give birth. He said: “The full diyah.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.اِسْتَهُ: his anus; here meaning control of the lower passage
key_terms.فَأَفْضَاهَا: he caused ifda' to her; a severe genital injury

ai.seo_question: When is the full diyah required for severe bodily injury in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on bodily injury compensation. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that in both the case of a man suffering a severe disabling injury and a slave-girl suffering a reproductive injury through ifda', the compensation is the full diyah.
